match.reason: No point in the bank covers the psychological influences on customer choice; the closest ones deal with the business environment, worker motivation or market research, which are different ideas.

draft.title: Psychological influences on customers
card: Perception
how a customer sees and makes sense of a product, its price, its packaging and its advertising. Two people can see the same product and form different views.
Motivation
the need or drive that pushes a customer to buy. A customer may buy a product to meet a need such as hunger, safety or being accepted by others.
Attitudes
the lasting likes, dislikes and beliefs a customer holds about a product or business. They tend to stay the same unless something changes the customer's mind.
Personality
a person's usual way of thinking and acting, such as being cautious or adventurous. It can shape which products and brands appeal to them.
draft.remember: Psychological influences come from inside the customer: how they see things, what drives them, what they believe and what they are like.

a.q: Priya has always believed that a certain brand of sports shoes is poorly made, so she avoids it. Which psychological influence is this?
opts: Her attitude to the brand
Her motivation to buy shoes
Her perception of the packaging
Her personality as a shopper
a.why: A lasting belief about a brand is an attitude. Motivation is the need that drives a purchase, and Priya's belief is not a need. Perception is how she sees something in front of her, not a settled belief she already holds.
a.clue: Look for a lasting belief about the brand.

b.q: Tom's Bakery in Bathurst moves its pies from a plain paper bag to a smart box. Customers now say the pies seem higher quality, though the recipe has not changed. Which influence does this show?
opts: Perception, as the box changed how customers see the pies
Attitude, as customers formed a lasting belief on the recipe
Motivation, as customers now need higher quality pies
Personality, as customers all became more adventurous eaters
b.why: The recipe is the same, but customers see the pies differently because of the packaging. That is perception. Attitude is tempting, but the change in view comes from how the pies look now, not from a long-held belief about the recipe.
b.clue: What changed: the product, or how customers see it?

b.best: Perception, as the box changed how customers see the pies
